inline_comments.comment: The `ax` parameter docstring says only 'Matplotlib subplot object' but does not document the new behavior: when `None`, a brand-new figure is created via `plt.subplots()`. The old behavior was to fall back to `plt.gca()`, so callers familiar with the previous semantics need an explicit description of what happens. Consider: 'ax : Axes, optional\n    Matplotlib axes to plot into. If None (default), a new Figure and\n    Axes are created and the Axes is returned.'

`plt.subplots()` (which allocates a new Figure) is called before the `isinstance(atoms, list)` guard on line 116. If the list has length != 1 the `assert` on line 117 raises `AssertionError`, leaving the newly created Figure object leaked with no reference. Swap the two blocks so input validation runs first, then create the figure only when the input is valid.

`plot_atoms_raw` does not replicate the `isinstance(atoms, list)` normalisation that `plot_atoms` applies before delegating here. Any caller who passes a single-element list directly to `plot_atoms_raw` will get a confusing `AttributeError` inside `PlottingVariables.__init__` (e.g., `list` has no `get_atomic_numbers`). Either add the same guard to `plot_atoms_raw` for robustness, or add an explicit note in its docstring that only an `Atoms` object (not a list) is accepted.

Both `plot_atoms` and `plot_atoms_raw` use NumPy-style docstrings with a `Parameters` section but are missing a `Returns` section. `plot_atoms` returns an `Axes` object, which callers depend on. Per ASE coding standards, the `Returns` section is required. Example addition for `plot_atoms`: `Returns
-------
Axes
    The Matplotlib Axes the atoms were plotted into.`

The section header is 'I/O', but the changes are to `ase/visualize/plot.py`, which is a visualization/plotting module, not an I/O format reader or writer. Looking at the scriv template, the correct section is 'GUI' (as used by, e.g., `20260318_172122_lempelto_gui_fg_color.rst`) or 'Other changes'.

general_comments.comment: No test for `plot_atoms_raw` is included. The existing `ase/test/test_matplotlib_plot.py` only exercises `plot_atoms`. Per project rules, at least one test exercising the new code path should be included before merging. A minimal test would verify that calling `plot_atoms_raw(atoms, ax)` populates `ax.patches` without calling `set_axis_off()`, confirming both that it draws atoms and that it leaves axis decorations intact.

The `animate` function (unchanged in this MR) calls `ax.axis('off')` immediately before `plot_atoms(atoms, ax=ax, ...)`. Now that `plot_atoms` always calls `ax.set_axis_off()` itself, the call inside `animate` is redundant. This is harmless but could confuse future readers into thinking `plot_atoms` does not manage axis visibility. A follow-up MR could remove the now-redundant call from `animate`, or switch `animate` to use `plot_atoms_raw` directly.
